name: claude-oss

config.written_by: commands/run/setup.md via oss:scheduler-step, probing the repo
keys_referenced: trap threshold for curate (key name unverified)

maintainer.summary: Owns release.authority when .oss.json says maintainer; types /oss:run once; reads the state file. Nowhere else in the loop.

scheduler.summary: The session the maintainer started. Runs /oss:run: diagnose, decide with next_action.py, spawn one step, read one handback, arm the next wakeup. Holds tag-and-publish authority by delegation to releaser only. Deliberately keeps no board summary so nothing stale is inherited.

scripts.name: scripts/next_action.py
scripts.purpose: rank what the repo needs now: unsafe | due(setup) | ranked | nothing-due; --take / --record-skip commit the choice

scripts.name: scripts/tick_handback.py
scripts.purpose: classify a sub-manager's framed final message into 7 states

scripts.name: scripts/release_handback.py
scripts.purpose: classify a releaser's final message into 4 states

scripts.name: scripts/triage_trigger.py
scripts.purpose: not-due | due | could-not-tell, from state file and last tag

scripts.name: scripts/oss_state.py
scripts.purpose: --decision 'triage sweep recorded' --triage-recorded, cohort burn-down --detail

scripts.name: scripts/agent_role.py
scripts.purpose: role marker under .git; the scheduler writes none

doctor.summary: Chase one WARN/FAIL line from doctor.sh past what the script fixes itself. Read-only intent, Bash grant total. Reports one line per line chased: repaired / not-ours / could-not-tell / could-not-repair.

scripts.name: scripts/doctor.sh
scripts.purpose: the diagnostic, findings-only mode

scripts.name: scripts/scaffold.py
scripts.purpose: --apply repairs an owned file
scripts.when: a line names an owned file

scripts.name: scripts/oss_config.py
scripts.purpose: read .oss.json

scheduler-step.summary: Run exactly one /oss:run sub-step (setup, scaffold, install-audit, triage, curate, changelog) by reading the one command file named in its prompt. Exists so the procedure's text never lands in the scheduler's long-lived context. Never dispatch, never release.

context.note: the one file its prompt names

scheduler-step._note: Per-step scripts belong to the command file it reads: setup -> oss_config.py, oss_state.py, scaffold.py; scaffold -> scaffold.py, release_version.py; install-audit -> doctor.sh, oss_config.py; triage -> board_touch.py, oss_state.py, statusline.py; curate -> trap_curate.py; changelog -> assemble_changelog.py.

sub-manager.summary: Run exactly one maintainer tick, then die. Re-derives the board itself. Spawns tick-dispatch first, then the developer lanes it rendered, then tick-review, tick-merge, tick-accounting. Holds merge authority; never tags, never publishes (role marker makes release_publish.py refuse). Reports TICK: completed | blocked | could-not-run | paused.

context.note: Skill(manager) as first act after the role marker
read in windows, past the truncation threshold

scripts.name: scripts/agent_role.py
scripts.purpose: --write sub-manager, first shell call; makes publish refuse

scripts.name: scripts/tick_handback.py
scripts.purpose: validate own draft handback before sending

scripts.name: scripts/agent_cost.py
scripts.purpose: measured context per lane, decides resume vs respawn-for-cost

scripts.name: scripts/release_publish.py
scripts.purpose: named only as the call that refuses under its marker

tick-dispatch.summary: Select, claim and render the dispatch payload for one tick, then die. Runs select_issues.py and lane_setup.py --claim per lane; hands back ready-to-paste Agent(...) calls. Has no Agent tool by design: the caller stays the live parent every lane's completion reaches.

scripts.name: scripts/select_issues.py
scripts.purpose: rank the board, group state per lane

scripts.name: scripts/lane_setup.py
scripts.purpose: --claim --phrase --subagent-type oss:developer --model sonnet: resolves base, branch, worktree and renders the lane's Agent(...) call

developer.summary: Implement one lane of up to three issues in a worktree: recon first, TDD, cross-platform audit, commit, then two reviewers, then spawn lane-report as the last act. Never pushes, never opens a PR. Spine file; late phases are separate files read when reached.

scripts.name: scripts/developer_phases.py
scripts.purpose: budgets of the phase files; fails if the spine stops naming one
scripts.when: CI, and named in the compliance survey

scripts.name: scripts/tree_snapshot.py
scripts.purpose: receipt that a read-only reviewer did not write into the worktree: clean | mutated | could-not-compare

scripts.name: scripts/review_return.py
scripts.purpose: frame and classify a reviewer's return; catches a return that carried nothing

scripts.name: scripts/fix_commit_scope.py
scripts.purpose: scope check on a fix commit after review

scripts.name: scripts/batch_hint.py
scripts.purpose: hook-side hint to batch supertool ops

scripts.name: scripts/assemble_changelog.py
scripts.purpose: changelog fragment shape it must leave

recon.summary: Read-only reconnaissance over one lane's issues: sites, nearest tests, siblings, file set. Under 2,500 words, ends with RECON-COST: <bash calls>. Never edits, never runs the suite, never decides the fix. Per part: confirmed-by-read / already-shipped / could-not-tell.

auditor.summary: Audit one committed diff against a fixed checklist of defect classes CI cannot fail on. Annotates, never blocks, writes nothing. Report opens with TREE: clean | mutated | could-not-compare, then one line per class: clean | finding | could not check.

context.note: shared with release-auditor, budgeted in scripts/audit_shared.py

scripts.name: scripts/tree_snapshot.py
scripts.purpose: the receipt its TREE: line reports

lane-report.summary: Compose one lane's note, JSON report (schemas/agent-report.schema.json) and pull request payload, then die. Derives diff, issue bodies and schema itself; the lane hands over only what it alone knows. Spawned by developer as its last act.

scripts.name: scripts/report_schema.py
scripts.purpose: validate the JSON report

scripts.name: scripts/agent_cost.py
scripts.purpose: cost figures for the report

tick-review.summary: Wait for CI on exactly the PR numbers it was given (pr_green.py --wait, one call per PR), then apply the maintainer's review checklist and route findings itself (file issue, comment, below-bar line). Reports REVIEW: reviewed (decision per PR: ready-to-merge | needs-fix) | pending | could-not-run. Inherits the sub-manager marker.

scripts.name: scripts/pr_green.py
scripts.purpose: --wait --timeout T per PR

scripts.name: scripts/tree_snapshot.py
scripts.purpose: receipt around review

tick-merge.summary: Merge exactly one reviewed PR: confirm-gated merge, post-merge obligations, default-branch recheck. Reports MERGE: merged | not-merged | could-not-run, plus a CURATE: line when merge.md says so. Inherits the sub-manager marker (merge allowed, publish refused).

scripts.name: scripts/lane_setup.py
scripts.purpose: named by merge.md for post-merge worktree cleanup (which flag: unverified)

tick-accounting.summary: Write the tick's state-file entry (oss_state.py --decision, lane fills, dispatch states, merge facts) and draft the validated TICK: handback block. Cannot send it: only the spawner's final message reaches the scheduler, so sub-manager pastes it verbatim. Reports ACCOUNTING: drafted | could-not-run.

scripts.name: scripts/oss_state.py
scripts.purpose: --decision with --lane-fill, --lane-dispatch-state, --detail; refuses an unreasoned short lane

scripts.name: scripts/tick_handback.py
scripts.purpose: validate the drafted block

triager.summary: Keep the tracker honest: priority, lane, milestone labels; surface what the board is lying about; name clusters one change would fix. POST labels, never PATCH. Never touches code, never closes an issue. Report is a table per issue plus refused list plus a required Clusters row: clusters | none | could not look.

scripts.name: scripts/ranking_table.py
scripts.purpose: the ranking rows it cites

releaser.summary: Run one release end to end from a fresh context: the six gates of commands/release.md, version sites, tag, publish. The only agent holding tag-and-publish authority, and only when release.authority in .oss.json is loop. Writes no role marker. Reports RELEASE: released | refused | could-not-run | paused.

context.note: the six gates; single source, not restated

scripts.name: scripts/release_delta.py
scripts.purpose: the delta since last tag

scripts.name: scripts/release_version.py
scripts.purpose: version sites

scripts.name: scripts/release_ci_wait.py
scripts.purpose: wait CI on the release commit

scripts.name: scripts/release_publish.py
scripts.purpose: tag + publish; refuses under a sub-manager marker

scripts.name: scripts/checklist_skew.py
scripts.purpose: gate check

scripts.name: scripts/cohort_citation_order.py
scripts.purpose: cohort label ordering

scripts.name: scripts/cohort_freeze_record.py
scripts.purpose: cohort label on every open issue at tag

scripts.name: scripts/plugin_update.py
scripts.purpose: plugin version bump

scripts.name: scripts/push_bypass.py
scripts.purpose: push past branch protection for the release commit

scripts.name: scripts/trap_curate.py
scripts.purpose: curate receipt

scripts.name: scripts/ranking_table.py
scripts.purpose: ranking rows in the audit payload

releaser._note: Scripts are commands/release.md's; the releaser owns them by following that file. It must NOT write a role marker (agent_role.py).

release-auditor.summary: Audit the whole delta since the last tag before it is tagged: composition defects no per-PR review sees. A release gate: could not run stops the release. Two rounds, hard cap. VERDICT: clean | findings | could not run.

scripts.name: scripts/release_delta.py
scripts.purpose: the range it audits

scripts.name: scripts/tree_snapshot.py
scripts.purpose: receipt that it wrote nothing

Explore.summary: Built-in read-only search agent, spawned by developer as the second reviewer alongside auditor.

declared_but_unrouted._comment: States and mentions that exist in prose with no edge above. A doctor would flag these; listed so the first reader run shows them rather than hides them.

items.note: Corrected 2026-09-19 after tracing. The spawn does exist in prose: dispatch.md:73 spells Agent(subagent_type: "oss:triager") and sub-manager reads that file — now edge run.21. The gap is one step later: the render path every tick actually uses (tick-dispatch → lane_setup.py --claim) hard-codes oss:developer, so no tick can produce a triager lane without hand-composing the call, which #989 forbids. Live triager spawns are the scheduler's only (run.04, run.06). Either retire the triager-lane rule from dispatch.md:45/73, or teach lane_setup.py a --subagent-type oss:triager the dispatcher can choose.

dispatch.md:55-62 tells the dispatcher to spawn oss:recon for --suggest-companions when it cannot name --lane patterns; since #1544 the dispatcher is tick-dispatch, whose frontmatter grants no Agent tool. Same shape as U1: a rule that survived the move of the step it governed.
TICK: paused and RELEASE: paused are resumed by SendMessage to the same agent, never a spawn. Not an edge; the reader should show it on the node.
commands/run/curate.md opens a PR from a scheduler-step; its handback shape is declared nowhere read.
